title: Delivery Claim Compensation Already Paid on Returned Units
content:
Marlowe & Finch never compensates a unit twice. When a Delivery Claims case has already paid compensation on an order line, and units of that line later come back on a Returns & Exchanges return, the compensation already paid is taken off the line's net unit price paid before the merchandise credit for the returned units is worked out.

## The rule

| What the Delivery Claims compensation entries show on the line | Taken off the net unit price paid, per unit |
|---|---|
| A merchandise refund paid on units of the line | That refund divided by the units it covered |
| No merchandise refund, but a Goodwill Credit given on the line | That Goodwill Credit divided by the units booked on the line |
| Neither a merchandise refund nor a Goodwill Credit on the line | Nothing more (0.00) |

- The records read are the claim's compensation-issued entries for the booking line: their compensation type (merchandise refund or Goodwill Credit), their amount and, for a merchandise refund, the units it covered.
- Where several merchandise refunds were paid on the line, the total refunded is divided by the total units those refunds covered.
- A merchandise refund on the line takes precedence: a Goodwill Credit is read only when no merchandise refund was paid on the line.
- The merchandise credit entered for the line is the one worked out after this deduction — the reduced net unit price times the accepted units, rounded half up to the cent — and it is that merchandise credit from which the line's sales tax credited is worked out.

## Basis questions

**A Delivery Claims merchandise refund of 36.00 USD covered 1 unit of a line whose net unit price paid is 72.00 USD. What is the merchandise credit for 1 accepted unit?** 36.00 divided by 1 is 36.00 taken off per unit, so 72.00 less 36.00 is 36.00 per unit; for 1 accepted unit the merchandise credit is 36.00. (Hypothetical figures.)

**A Goodwill Credit of 20.00 USD was given on a line booked with 4 units at a net unit price paid of 45.00 USD, with no merchandise refund. What is taken off?** 20.00 divided by the 4 units booked is 5.00 per unit, leaving 40.00 per unit; 2 accepted units are credited 80.00. (Hypothetical figures.)

**Does the Goodwill Credit count if the same line also received a merchandise refund?** No. With a merchandise refund on the line, only that refund, divided by the units it covered, is taken off.

**A line with no claim compensation at all?** Nothing more is taken off its net unit price paid.
